correctness.rationale: The preimage of any successful singleton is a nonempty cyclic interval. Inverse b produces a unit gain exactly at start 0, a loss exactly at start n-k, and otherwise no change; inverse a rotates the start. Consecutive gains force n-1 rotations. The length lower bound L+t+(n+1)h+r excludes loss at L+1, reducing all possibilities to two boundary a insertions or exactly one no-op b. Counting safe phases gives (n-2)^2+1 b variants and two a variants. Forward subset DP independently confirms counts for 3<=n<=13 and brute-force literal words for n=3,4,5; the symbolic argument proves all n>=3.

A full optimal-plus-one word classification exposes a forbidden inverse-arc phase and a quadratic multiplicity phenomenon.
